newsitem.title: FINLAND: Baltic Ice-New restrictions due in Gulf of Finland.
newsitem.headline: Baltic Ice-New restrictions due in Gulf of Finland.

text.p: Ice thickened slightly and new restrictions were due in the eastern Gulf of Finland, the Finnish Institute of Marine Research said on Monday.
It said only ships with ice-classes I and II with deadweights over 1,300 tonnes would be assisted to Inkoo, Kantvik, Helsinki and Porvoo from February 28.
The restriction for Loviisa, Kotka and Hamina would be lifted to ice-classes IA and IB with 1,300 deadweight tonnes, or IC and II with 2,000 deadweight tonnes on February 28, it said.

Swedish restrictions for the northern Gulf of Bothnia would be lifted to ice class IA and 3,000 deadweight tonnes on February 26 and the restriction for Ornskoldsvik would be lifted to ice-class IC and 1,300 tonnes, an institute spokesman said.

Four icebreakers were on station near St Petersburg and Vyborg in the eastern Gulf of Finland, one near Porvoo and Loviisa, four in the northern end of the Gulf of Bothnia, two in the middle, and one outside Rauma.
One ice-breaker remained on station in the Gulf of Riga.

NOTES: New ice - forming, thin and still moving. Fast ice - not moving level flat ice. Level ice - thick flat ice. Consolidated/compact - compact close ice. Windrow ice - reshaped by wind, thickness varies sharply. Rafted - ridges forming, 10-20 cm thick. Ridged - ridged or hummocked ice. Open - floes with water at rate of 4-6:10. Close ice - floes tightly packed.
